title: Declarative stream router + lightweight event checkpoint playbook for Python SDK
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers find it hard to write robust streaming chat consumers that handle partial events (delta tokens, tool call begin/end, structured JSON chunks), perform idempotent resume after interruptions, and implement retries without duplicating handling logic. Current idioms in the SDK are low-level (raw event streams or baked-in high-level helpers) which either leak implementation details or are rigid for integration needs.

Goal: Ship a documented, small-surface API that: (1) provides a declarative routing DSL for stream event shapes, (2) offers lightweight checkpoint tokens that let apps resume from the last processed event without reprocessing side effects, (3) standardizes retry semantics (idempotent vs non-idempotent) and backoff hooks, and (4) emits telemetry spans and tokenized cost/latency metrics for observability.

Scope: Python SDK surface only (backwards-compatible additions). Implement router + checkpoint envelope + examples + unit/integration tests + migration guidance. No server changes required. Rollout gated by API review and API compatibility tests.

Non-goal: Replacing existing advanced stream frameworks or fully implementing resumable transactional sinks inside the SDK. We provide primitives, patterns, and a canonical implementable reference.

Motivation/Context: Several customer support cases and internal bugs show frequent mistakes: double-invocation of side-effecting callbacks on resume, subtle ordering bugs when mixing structured output events with text deltas, and surprising latency spikes when users naively buffer whole responses before processing. The platform already emits token-level telemetry; we want to make it easy for apps to correlate stream processing decisions with cost/latency and to enable safer retries.

Reference: design doc (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/py-stream-router-design, PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/1487 (WIP), internal benchmark: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/py-router-compare
acceptance_criteria: Public API: `StreamRouter` class + decorator helpers (`@router.on('text_delta')`, `@router.on('json_chunk')`, `@router.on('tool_call')`) with documented signatures
Checkpoint token format stable (opaque base64 string containing sequence id + verification hash) and documented to interop across SDK versions
Resume semantics: idempotent handlers supported via `@router.idempotent` marker; examples show safe retry strategies for external side effects
Retry integration: SDK exposes pluggable backoff policy hook and retry callback that receives last checkpoint token
Telemetry: produced spans/tags for stream start/end, per-chunk processing latency, and checkpoint creation with token size/cost metadata
End-to-end tests: unit tests and a small integration test with a local mock server verifying resume and non-duplication of side effects
Docs and migration guide merged (docs site + examples in examples/streaming/ resume-safe-consumer.py)
API review completed and no breaking changes introduced to existing streaming APIs

decisions: Design: checkpoint token will be opaque base64 envelope containing: last_event_seq (int), truncated-event-hash (sha256 hex prefix), sdk_version tag. We keep token opaque to allow format changes with versioning
Handlers: make handler functions async-capable. Provide sync wrapper for convenience. Avoid forcing users into async-only API
Idempotency: declare idempotency via decorator instead of implicit heuristics. SDK will not attempt to dedupe side effects for the user
Retries: SDK retry hook will retry entire streaming call unless user supplies a resume token. Default behavior: on transient network errors, do not auto-resume for non-idempotent handlers
Telemetry: attach token metadata to spans, but do not include sensitive payloads in traces
tradeoffs: Opaque token vs structured token: opaque simplifies evolution but hides debuggability. Mitigation: docs include a token-inspector helper for local debugging only
Providing high-level guaranteed exactly-once semantics would require server-side support and external coordination; chosen approach is pragmatic: idempotent markers + guidance
Sync wrapper increases API surface and maintenance cost but reduces friction for synchronous apps
